name: icon
description:
One glyph from the registry, at a size and a tone the system names. Every icon on every surface is this — the geometry lives once in `icons.avenceo.json` and a view supplies only a name, because the engine's tag allowlist admits no SVG and loosening it would let a view emit script. What this unit adds is the part the registry deliberately does not hold: how big, and in what colour, since geometry has no opinion about either.

The interface follows the practices the Iconify ecosystem settled on — 1em box, currentColor, a -0.125em baseline seat, flips and quarter-turns as transforms rather than duplicate drawings — plus one house rule Iconify leaves to callers: directional icons declare `mirror: rtl` and follow the reading direction themselves.

base.$description: Sized in `em`, so an icon inside a control scales with that control rather than being pinned to a pixel value that is right in one place and wrong in the next. The DEFAULT is `lg` at 2rem — the type scale here tops out at 38px and bottoms at 9px, so an icon matched to body text lands at 13px, which is smaller than any glyph with a duotone backing can carry. An icon set inline beside a sentence should ask for `sm`. `flex-shrink:0` because a glyph is never the thing that should give way in a tight row.

size.$description: A ladder in rem rather than in type steps, because an icon is a shape and the type scale is a reading ladder — matching them made every icon smaller than the thing it labelled.

tone.$description: An icon inherits `currentColor` by default, which is right almost everywhere — it is part of the sentence it sits in. These are for the cases where it is not: a status glyph that must carry its own meaning.

flip.$description: Reuse one drawing four ways instead of registering four drawings — the practice every mature icon interface (Iconify's hFlip/vFlip among them) settled on, because a mirrored upload is a download and a set that stores both drifts in one of them. A transform costs nothing and cannot drift.

rotate.$description: Quarter turns, same reasoning as flip: one chevron is every chevron.

mirror.$description: Opt-in RTL awareness, and the one place this leaf goes past Iconify: Iconify leaves direction to the caller, and the caller forgets. A DIRECTIONAL icon — an arrow that means forward, a chevron that means deeper — declares `mirror: rtl` and flips itself under `[dir="rtl"]`, so the geometry follows the reading direction without any call site knowing the locale. A glyph whose shape is meaning (a checkmark, a brand mark) simply never declares it. This is `accessibility/i18n-rtl.md` made structural, and it is what `verify_rtl` cannot check for icons any other way.

placement.$description: `block` clears the baseline shift for an icon standing alone — a crest in a header, a glyph centred in an empty state. The default is inline, nudged -0.125em, because an icon in a sentence sits ON the baseline like a letter (Iconify's `inline` behaviour, made the default here since that is where icons actually live).

a11y.note: Decorative by default — `aria-hidden`, because an icon beside a label that already says the word makes a screen reader say it twice. Give it a `title` ONLY when the icon is the whole message, at which point it becomes `role=img` with a label. An icon-only button is the other case: the label belongs on the button, not on the glyph inside it. Colour is never the only signal: a red error glyph needs the word too.
